statutory.question: Does the conduct described fall within 5318(g)?
statutory.label: entailment
statutory.reasoning: 31 U.S.C. § 5318(g) requires a financial institution to file a suspicious activity report when it knows, suspects, or has reason to suspect that a transaction involves suspicious activity. The entity’s declared monthly volume of $615,037 is far below the $2,403,128.89 wire on 2026-04-18, and the note describes over-invoiced trade-finance, a classic red flag. The subsequent transfers of $226,642.20, $146,804.69, and $192,591.40 to Singapore entities also support a pattern of structuring and potential trade-based money laundering. These facts satisfy each element of the statutory reporting trigger. Yes it does
